svg.text: The create hot path — what fast-sandbox removes
Both paths persist durable intent; only the per-sandbox scheduling machinery differs.
Per-pod backend (per sandbox)
API write → scheduler → watch propagation → kubelet
reconciliation → runtime start (± image pull)
every sandbox pays the full Kubernetes machinery again;
pools remove the pod start, not the per-sandbox write path
Fast Sandbox (per sandbox)
one CRD write (durable intent) → in-memory placement
→ atomic admission into a warm Fastlet → containerd
starts the runtime directly
no scheduler, no watch wait, no kubelet — the cluster keeps
doing what it is good at: Fastlet pods, accounting, pool scheduling
Admission, step by step
1 · rank in-memory candidates (image-cache affinity,
then load, then stable hash)
2 · persist one Sandbox CR — the complete initial intent
3 · atomic admission on the chosen Fastlet; network slot
and policy bindings arrive before the runtime does
4 · runtime starts from pre-pulled artifacts (warm images
are protected from cache eviction)
the network slot exists before the sandbox: no per-create
setup window, and policy can be late but never open
same durability, less machinery
